_schema: Each row: id, class(live|filing|event), value, status(clear|amber|red|watch), proposed_status, rationale, confidence(high|medium|low), series_id, source, citation(URL), as_of(YYYY-MM-DD), next_release. RULES: (1) live/filing status is derived deterministically from value vs trigger. (2) event rows — the agent may self-promote clear->amber WITH a citation; amber->red and any de-escalation go in proposed_status for user confirm, never in status. (3) No citation => no status change on event/filing rows (the console rejects it). (4) confidence defaults to 'medium' if unstated. (5) reputable secondary sources (Reuters/BBG/FT) are acceptable when the primary isn't out yet.
_paste_note: The agent writes only the mutable fields (value, status, proposed_status, rationale, confidence, citation, as_of, next_release). The console holds the static definitions (names, conditions, guardrails, trigger). Paste this whole object, or just a {"asOf":..,"posture":..,"rows":[..]} with the ids you changed.

notes: WSHR (30% core) is ballast vs equity/AI-demand crash but is the MOST rate-shock-exposed sleeve (stable-compounder cohort de-rates on rising real rates — the Patel/Winton/El-Erian crowding-out victims). True hedges for the rate-shock scenario = cash (>10%, on top) + gold, NOT WSHR. In a rate shock, WSHR + growth + rate-sensitive software soften together; cash is the only clean ballast.
